allow_large: The owner asked to move every Forge install to PyPI after GitHub disabled the old repo; the nine files are the install strings, the two install scripts, the plugin marketplace and the package metadata.
done_when: Every install, upgrade, hook fallback and pinned-release command Forge prints or generates uses symphony-forge==<version> from PyPI and no command names the knacklabs GitHub repo, the plugin marketplace points at vrknetha/symphony-forge, and the package metadata carries the README and the project links so the PyPI page shows them.

known.title: Provide a bootstrap path for existing clients' upgrade checks
Make historical pinned releases available on PyPI
Find the newest release from a source that publishes releases
Preserve the user's plugin settings when moving the marketplace
Make README documentation links work on the PyPI page
Persist the recovery release before merging the upgrade

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a client with Forge v1.2.48 installed follows the recovery steps.
The documented `uvx` command runs Forge from a disposable environment whose executable directory is placed first on PATH by [uv's tool runner](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.12.0/crates/uv/src/commands/tool/run.rs#L334-L344). Consequently, `_on_path()` sees the requested release and `src/forge/upgrade.py:101,235–236` skips the persistent install. After `uvx` exits, the old Forge remains installed. Once the owner merges and updates the default branch, that CLI routes state-changing commands through the disabled GitHub source for the new pin (`v1.2.48:src/forge/repo.py:983–991,1015–1019`), so normal Forge work fails. This PATH behavior is new evidence against the ruling that the newer release recovers old pins. The recovery test starts Forge directly and then manually installs a new launcher (`tests/test_package_installs_from_pypi.py:80,100`), so it misses the failure.
findings.title: Persist the recovery release before merging the upgrade

why: GitHub disabled the knacklabs repo, so every Forge install and upgrade line that points at git+https://github.com/knacklabs/symphony-forge@<version> fails in client CI, hooks and the pinned-release runner; Forge is now published on PyPI as symphony-forge, and its PyPI page shows no description.
